chunk_map.heading: Exercise: Write your team notes (H1 + lede)
Write a few lines per person

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "Mark where you are guessing": line 34: "Those are the first gaps the memory will show you" is the closest. "the memory" is not named in this file, but the enclosing module see-your-team.md What You'll Learn names "a leadership memory" (module signposting counts as prior context per the carve-out). "Those" resolves to the two or three people named one line up. Line 6 "the page every agent in this training reads" resolves to team-notes.md in the same sentence.

grep of body for positional callbacks (opening lecture|earlier lecture|the prework|previous exercise) -> 0 hits. Closest: line 15 "You will rate again later in the training" points forward by claim, not by file position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw/caught" in body. Closest line 24 "The reorg, the new tool, the process that came and went" is generic examples of change, not a beat reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no live-demo guess/reveal beat; the only quoted specimen (line 26) is an example note, and every slide opens on a verbed sentence

rules_evaluated.evidence: Smallest chunk 3 "Mark where you are guessing" lines 30-34 carries a self-contained claim: leave thin blocks thin and list the two or three people you know least about.

chunk 2 "Write a few lines per person" (line 17) is a true summary of the four bolded field leads at lines 21-24; chunk 1 "Rate your confidence first" matches line 13 "Line one is a number". Closest: chunk 3 header "Mark where you are guessing" covers the thin-blocks and least-known-people content.

Per chunk: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." (line 22 "not what you assume" is a single contrast); no anaphora triple; no self-grading superlative; no number+retraction; no abstraction-noun stack. Closest line 28 "who they trust, who they teach, who they would follow": three concrete, distinct legs, each answers "what does this mean" alone.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n -i -E "\b(beat|mood|firing|compendium|forcing function|surface)\b" over body -> 0 hits (the two hits are in the maintainer block, lines 40-41). "blocks" and "memory" are ordinary engineer vocabulary here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 2 lines 21-24 carry four bolded labels, the named fields of the checklist the student fills per person (checklist item names are handles under the rule); no bold sentence continues past its label. Closest: line 24 "**What the last change left them believing.**" is 7 words, over the 5-word handle guide, but is still a label not a lead sentence. Chunk 0 bold labels (lines 5-7) are the exercise header template.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Included by standalone-paragraph link "[Exercise: Write your team notes](exercises/write-your-team-notes.md)" in trainings/engineering-management/see-your-team.md under "## Write down what only you know"; exercise content reaches the composed deck through the phase--exercise wrapper. Rendering not run; verified from include structure and check-slide-size reporting slides: 3.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no Phase N / Step N headers or in-body phase references; check-slide-numbering.js -> OK, 59 files consistent

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --report -> 0 entries for this file. Closest: line 32 "add a line at the bottom of the file" points at the student's own team-notes.md, not at the slide or page; line 26 "announced from above" is organisational, inside a quoted example.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no links in body; rule is a review surface, not a gate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise ## headings are imperative: line 9 "Rate your confidence first", line 17 "Write a few lines per person", line 30 "Mark where you are guessing". No law or consolidation slide, so no claim heading is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 28 "Nobody else can write these lines." is a short kicker, but it carries the reason the manager writes them and does not restate the header or the line 7 point ("An agent can reason about your people only as well as you describe them"), so it is not class (c). Line 15 "You will rate again later in the training, against this one." adds an object (the later comparison).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no header rename trigger: one commit in history for the file, and no maintainer provenance note of the (from <old-file>, header his) shape
